chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman whose husband died and he had not entered into marital relations with her. He (The Imam) said: 'For her is the inheritance, and upon her is the complete waiting period (iddah). And if he had specified a dower for her, then for her is half of it. And if he had not specified a dower for her, then there is nothing for her.'
ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance and dower rights of a widow if her husband died before marital consummation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal precedent for a widow whose husband died before consummation, affirming her right to a full wife's inheritance share and the complete four-month waiting period (iddah). It further clarifies the dower (mahr) entitlement: she receives half of the agreed amount if specified, or nothing if unspecified, reflecting the principle that consummation validates the full financial bond. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between the rights of 'dakhilah' (consummated) and 'ghayr dakhilah' (non-consummated) wives.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a woman whose husband died and he had not slept with her. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For her is the inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period; and if a dower has been specified for her, so for her would be half of it, and if a dower has not been specified for her, so there is nothing for her’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman whose husband dies before going to bed with her. He (the Imam) said, ‘She inherits and must count the waiting period, if mahr (dower) was set for her she deserved one-half of it, otherwise, she does not have the right to demand mahr (dower).”’
